scope: Focused independent mathematical and exact-source review of HTS3–HTS5. HTS4 is the finite-character consumer actually used in TwistOk, not a new proof of the more general arbitrary-weight TwAwayAlt statement.
findings: HTS3 correctly obtains rank-one cuspidal support from character-valued inertia type: a Weil/inertia commutator has all eigenvalues one, its irreducible constituent has semisimple inertia, inertia is central, and a Frobenius eigenline forces rank one. This gives the literal GoodCusp rank-one disjunction. The total support polynomial is one on every Weil commutator, and N=0 supplies both Gd fields. No genericity or PlainTor is asserted.

For spherical untwisting HTS3 uses GUA12 at its full spherical scope. Untwisting its support gives Good before invoking the guarded IsRecT twist law. Scalar twisting preserves zero monodromy and the commutator polynomial, for every correspondence.

HTS4 preserves an actual IsWDOf witness. Intersecting its open inertia subgroup with the finite character kernel preserves the same N; raw Weil action is multiplied by the character. In IsFrobSS both commuting operators are scaled by the same nonzero scalar, so commutation and nilpotence of their difference persist. The full inertia action is retained, not merely its semisimplification. The Artin character and algNorm shifts agree under the original Good guard.

HTS5 explicitly assumes a smooth irreducible subquotient after the requested clarity correction. Inverse finite parts and surjective Artin on units give pairwise distinct unit characters; hence the exact totally disjoint product theorem applies, excluding all unramified norm shifts. The inducing-function map f(g) -> kappa(det(g))f(g) has the correct intertwining orientation.

HTS5 multiplies the ordinary character identity by the weight-zero Artin identity. The new finite part is phi_i times the inverse restricted twisting character, with open kernel; all algebraic weights and index orders remain unchanged.

HTS6 was also read for interface compatibility and uses HAW10 with the actual arbitrary part-dependent predicate and the same x and Hecke data; this observation is supplementary, not an independent full review of HTS6.
corrections_resolved: HTS5 statement now explicitly specifies smooth irreducibility of the subquotient, as required by its proof.
limitations: Retained local classification, full IsRecT laws, original reciprocity and monodromy foundations are not reproved or recertified here.
This focused review does not certify HTS1–2 or HTS6–8. No Lean replay.
